source.original_text:
The actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian mixtures have nonnegative measurable Lebesgue-integrable densities of mass one. P_b(dx)=q_b(x)\,dx,\qquad q_b\ge0,\quad q_b\in L^1(dx),\quad\int q_b(x)\,dx=1,\qquad b\in\{-1,+1\}. Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including both endpoints and odd dimensions. Every \(n/2\) is a real exponent. \(\mu\) is the canonical full-orthogonal Haar probability and \(
u_b=2\mu\!estriction\{\det O=b\}\). The actual mixture is \(P_b=
u_b\mathrm{bind}\gamma\), where \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\). The source density \(p_b\) is determined only Lebesgue-a.e. We choose the literal average \(q_b\) below and certify it by equality of actual measures. No pointwise equality to a different arbitrary source representative is asserted. Pointwise inner absolute integrability, measurability, matrix positivity, actual mixture probability, outer L1, normalization and the measure identity are proved inside the theorem. None is a caller hypothesis; totalized Bochner integration supplies no fallback value. A_O= rac{\kappa+1}{2}I- rac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^	op),\quad\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1}),\quad p_O(x)= rac{\sqrt{\det A_O}}{(2\pi)^{n/2}}\exp\!\left(- rac{x^	op A_Ox}{2}ight). 
u_b=2\mu\!estriction\{\det O=b\},\quad P_b=
u_b\mathrm{bind}\gamma,\quad q_b(x)=\int p_O(x)\,d
u_b(O).

∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ),
    let μ := (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))))⁻¹
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)))).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
    let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
    (∀ x, 0 ≤ qpos x ∧ 0 ≤ qneg x) ∧
    Measurable qpos ∧ Measurable qneg ∧
    Integrable qpos volume ∧ Integrable qneg volume ∧
    (∫ x, qpos x) = 1 ∧ (∫ x, qneg x) = 1 ∧
    νpos.bind γ = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (qpos x)) ∧
    νneg.bind γ = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (qneg x))
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard l2 norm, Borel structure and Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Fin n indexes coordinates from zero through n-1. WithLp.ofLp is the coordinate representation.

The orthogonal group is full real O(n), both determinant signs, with its matrix Borel structure. Measure.haarMeasure(top : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts G) is canonical normalized full-group Haar probability.

Measure.restrict is restriction to the displayed set. Scalar multiplication of measures uses extended nonnegative real scalars. Measure.bind integrates the displayed measure kernel against its input measure. Measure.withDensity of a nonnegative extended-real function is the measure whose measurable-set values are its set lintegrals under the base measure.

multivariateGaussian mean m matrix C is the pushforward of canonical stdGaussian by z -> m + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. Its covariance interpretation holds for positive semidefinite C. Matrix inverse is standard totalized matrix inverse.

Integrable is genuine real Bochner absolute integrability. The displayed integrals with real integrands are real Bochner integrals; unspecified measure is volume on the displayed Euclidean carrier. Real n/2 powers use Real.rpow and real division; natural powers have natural exponents. ENNReal.ofReal maps a real number to its nonnegative extended-real truncation. Real division/inverse are totalized at zero.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianMixtureLaws
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LocallyIntegrable

/-!
# Actual mixed Gaussian densities

The density notation of Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2
introduction and B.2.3, is realized by actual conditioned-Haar averages.
The chosen representatives are nonnegative measurable Lebesgue L1 functions
of mass one and define exactly the actual Gaussian bind mixtures.
Source densities are a.e. objects; no pointwise equality to a different
arbitrary source representative is asserted. Pointwise inner L1 is proved,
so totalized Bochner integration is not used as a fallback.
TV/affinity comparison, Eq25, products and amplification remain separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.MixtureDensities
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem actual_mixture_densities {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let μ := orthogonalHaar n
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
    let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
    (∀ x, 0 ≤ qpos x ∧ 0 ≤ qneg x) ∧
    Measurable qpos ∧ Measurable qneg ∧
    Integrable qpos volume ∧ Integrable qneg volume ∧
    (∫ x, qpos x) = 1 ∧ (∫ x, qneg x) = 1 ∧
    νpos.bind γ = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (qpos x)) ∧
    νneg.bind γ = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (qneg x)) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let G := Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  let μ := orthogonalHaar n
  let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : G | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
  let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : G | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
  let γ : G → Measure E := fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : E)
    (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
  let p : G → E → ℝ := fun O x =>
    Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det / (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  have hlaws := GaussianMixtureLaws.actual_mixture_laws hn hκ
  have hγ : Measurable γ := hlaws.1
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure (νpos.bind γ) := hlaws.2.1
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure (νneg.bind γ) := hlaws.2.2.1
  have hpriors := DeterminantComponents.component_probabilities
    (lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn)
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure νpos := hpriors.2.2.1
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure νneg := hpriors.2.2.2
  have hAc : Continuous (fun O : G => singleBlockPrecision κ O) := by
    unfold singleBlockPrecision
    exact continuous_const.sub
      ((continuous_subtype_val.add continuous_subtype_val.matrix_transpose).const_smul
        ((κ - 1) / 4))
  have hpc : Continuous (Function.uncurry p) := by
    dsimp only [p, Function.uncurry, E]
    fun_prop
  have hp0 (O : G) (x : E) : 0 ≤ p O x := by dsimp [p]; positivity
  have hd (O : G) : γ O = (volume : Measure E).withDensity
      (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (p O x)) :=
    GaussianLawDensity.gaussian_law_eq_density hn hκ O
  -- One internal construction is used for each of the two actual priors.
  have hdata (ν : Measure G) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
      [IsProbabilityMeasure (ν.bind γ)] :
      let q : E → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂ν
      (∀ x, 0 ≤ q x) ∧ Measurable q ∧ Integrable q volume ∧
        (∫ x, q x) = 1 ∧
        ν.bind γ = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (q x)) := by
    let q : E → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂ν
    have hpi (x : E) : Integrable (fun O => p O x) ν := by
      have hpx : Continuous (fun O : G => p O x) :=
        hpc.comp (continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const)
      simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using
        (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact (μ := ν) isCompact_univ hpx.continuousOn)
    have hq0 (x : E) : 0 ≤ q x := integral_nonneg (fun O => hp0 O x)
    have hqm : Measurable q :=
      (hpc.stronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_left (μ := ν)).measurable
    have hpm : Measurable (Function.uncurry (fun O x => ENNReal.ofReal (p O x))) :=
      ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp hpc.measurable
    have hmeasure : ν.bind γ = (volume : Measure E).withDensity
        (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (q x)) := by
      apply Measure.ext
      intro B hB
      rw [Measure.bind_apply hB hγ.aemeasurable, withDensity_apply _ hB]
      calc
        (∫⁻ O, γ O B ∂ν) =
            ∫⁻ O, (∫⁻ x in B, ENNReal.ofReal (p O x) ∂(volume : Measure E)) ∂ν := by
          apply lintegral_congr
          intro O
          rw [hd O, withDensity_apply _ hB]
        _ = ∫⁻ x in B, (∫⁻ O, ENNReal.ofReal (p O x) ∂ν) ∂(volume : Measure E) :=
          lintegral_lintegral_swap hpm.aemeasurable
        _ = ∫⁻ x in B, ENNReal.ofReal (q x) := by
          apply lintegral_congr
          intro x
          exact (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal (hpi x)
            (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun O => hp0 O x))).symm
    have hmassNN : (∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (q x)) = 1 := by
      have hu := congrArg (fun M : Measure E => M Set.univ) hmeasure
      simpa only [measure_univ, withDensity_apply _ MeasurableSet.univ,
        Measure.restrict_univ] using hu.symm
    have hqi : Integrable q volume :=
      (lintegral_ofReal_ne_top_iff_integrable hqm.aestronglyMeasurable
        (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hq0)).mp (by rw [hmassNN]; exact ENNReal.one_ne_top)
    have hmass : (∫ x, q x) = 1 := by
      rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae
        (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hq0) hqm.aestronglyMeasurable, hmassNN]
      simp
    exact ⟨hq0, hqm, hqi, hmass, hmeasure⟩
  have hpos := hdata νpos
  have hneg := hdata νneg
  exact ⟨(fun x => ⟨hpos.1 x, hneg.1 x⟩), hpos.2.1, hneg.2.1,
    hpos.2.2.1, hneg.2.2.1, hpos.2.2.2.1, hneg.2.2.2.1,
    hpos.2.2.2.2, hneg.2.2.2.2⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.MixtureDensities

notation.text: A is the literal precision; its inverse is covariance. The Euclidean dot product and Lebesgue volume are the same ones used by the canonical actual Gaussian-density producer.
Both signs use the same full O(n) Haar law. The real Bochner average defines the selected representative at every x; its genuine inner L1 is established internally.

steps.title: Fix the actual component and mixture laws
steps.text: The source conditioned priors have mass one. Reuse the canonical actual-mixture construction and the exact Gaussian precision-density identity.
steps.lean: hlaws calls GaussianMixtureLaws.actual_mixture_laws; hpriors calls DeterminantComponents.component_probabilities. hd calls GaussianLawDensity.gaussian_law_eq_density. The notation P_b is a measure on Euclidean space; no prior or Gaussian law is supplied as an abstract witness.

steps.title: Establish each finite average
steps.text: For every fixed x, O↦p_O(x) is continuous on compact O(n), so it is genuinely absolutely integrable under the finite conditioned prior. This is an explicit internal construction omitted by the paper. It uses continuity/compactness; the independently retained source envelope is another sufficient route, not a theorem this proof calls.
steps.formula: \forall x,\quad O\mapsto p_O(x)\in L^1(\nu_b),\qquad q_b(x)=\int p_O(x)\,d\nu_b(O)\in\mathbb R.
steps.lean: hAc and hpc prove actual joint continuity. hpi applies ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact to each slice and the whole compact group. No nonintegrable-integral default is used.

steps.title: Keep the representatives nonnegative and measurable
steps.text: The component density is nonnegative. Integrating a nonnegative function gives a nonnegative average, and joint measurability gives measurability of the parameterized integral.
steps.lean: hp0 and integral_nonneg give hq0. hqm consumes StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_left from the actual joint density.

steps.title: Identify the actual mixture density
steps.text: For any measurable Euclidean event B, first use the actual bind evaluation and actual component law-density identity. Tonelli exchanges nonnegative integration. The proved inner L1 identifies the ENNReal integral with ofReal of the real average.
steps.lean: hmeasure uses Measure.ext, Measure.bind_apply, withDensity_apply, lintegral_lintegral_swap and ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal. Both measures of each nested integral are explicit.

steps.title: Produce genuine outer L1 and mass one
steps.text: Evaluate the actual probability measure at the entire Euclidean space. The nonnegative density integral is exactly one and therefore finite. Measurability and this finite integral give true Bochner L1, followed by the real normalization.
steps.lean: hmassNN is the univ evaluation of hmeasure, using actual mixture probability from hlaws. hqi uses lintegral_ofReal_ne_top_iff_integrable. hmass uses integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae and ENNReal.toReal_one.

steps.title: Consume the actual densities in affinity
steps.text: Apply the produced nonnegativity, measurability, L1 and masses to the actual representatives for both signs. Their square roots lie in L2. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the source initial affinity bound and genuine integrability. The consumer also retains both actual law-density equalities.

reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n, and then for every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, make the following local definitions. The Lean binder order is implicit n : ℕ, explicit hn : 3 ≤ n, implicit κ : ℝ, explicit hκ : 4 ≤ κ. The names hn and hκ denote proofs of the displayed inequalities; there are no further hypotheses.

Let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), the standard real n-dimensional Euclidean space, with coordinates indexed by Fin n = {0, …, n−1}, its standard l2 norm and Borel structure, and its Euclidean Lebesgue measure volume. Let G = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, the full real orthogonal group O(n), with its matrix Borel structure. For O ∈ G, write M_O for its underlying real n-by-n matrix, and write v_x = WithLp.ofLp x for the coordinate vector of x ∈ E. These are expository abbreviations, not extra quantified inputs.

Let μ be Measure.haarMeasure applied to the top positive compact of G; by the supplied definition context this is the canonical normalized Haar probability measure on the full group G. Define measures on that same carrier G by
νpos = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det M_O = 1}),
νneg = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • (μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det M_O = −1}).
Thus the factors 2 are extended nonnegative real scalars multiplying restricted measures. Neither restricted measure has a different subtype as its carrier.

For O ∈ G, put
A_O = ((κ + 1)/2) • I_n − ((κ − 1)/4) • (M_O + M_Oᵀ),
where I_n is the real n-by-n identity matrix, the two coefficients are real numbers, and the operations • are real scalar multiplication of matrices. In entries,
(A_O)ᵢⱼ = ((κ + 1)/2) δᵢⱼ − ((κ − 1)/4)((M_O)ᵢⱼ + (M_O)ⱼᵢ)
for every i,j ∈ Fin n. This abbreviation is the same matrix in both following definitions.

Let γ : G → Measure E be defined by
γ(O) = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : E) (A_O⁻¹).
The inverse is Lean's standard totalized matrix inverse. The supplied convention for multivariateGaussian m C is the pushforward of the canonical standard Gaussian on E under z ↦ m + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. Consequently the exact matrix argument here is C = A_O⁻¹: it is this inverse that is subjected to the matrix square root in the definition. The supplied covariance interpretation applies when C is positive semidefinite. This explains the convention and does not add a positive-semidefiniteness hypothesis or conclusion to the displayed theorem.

Let p : G → E → ℝ be the real-valued function
p(O,x) = [Real.sqrt(det A_O) / (2π)^((n : ℝ)/2)] · Real.exp(−[v_x ⬝ᵥ (A_O *ᵥ v_x)]/2).
Here ⬝ᵥ is the real coordinate dot product and *ᵥ is matrix-vector multiplication, so the quadratic form is Σᵢ Σⱼ (v_x)ᵢ (A_O)ᵢⱼ (v_x)ⱼ. The scalar Real.sqrt is applied to det A_O, and the denominator is (2 * Real.pi) raised using Real.rpow to the real exponent (n : ℝ)/2. In particular the exponent is real division by 2 even when n is odd; it is not a natural-number exponent or truncated natural division. The exponential has exponent minus the quadratic form divided by the real number 2. Real scalar division and inverse use the totalized conventions supplied in the packet.

Finally let qpos, qneg : E → ℝ be
qpos(x) = ∫ O, p(O,x) ∂νpos,
qneg(x) = ∫ O, p(O,x) ∂νneg.
These are real Bochner integrals over the full group carrier G with the indicated measures, not extended-real integrals. Their definitions themselves do not insert an additional integrability hypothesis.

For these local definitions, the conclusion is exactly the conjunction of the following nine clauses, in this order:
(1) For every x ∈ E, both 0 ≤ qpos(x) and 0 ≤ qneg(x).
(2) qpos is measurable.
(3) qneg is measurable.
(4) qpos is integrable with respect to volume on E.
(5) qneg is integrable with respect to volume on E.
(6) ∫ x, qpos(x) ∂volume = 1.
(7) ∫ x, qneg(x) ∂volume = 1.
(8) νpos.bind γ = volume.withDensity (x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal(qpos(x))).
(9) νneg.bind γ = volume.withDensity (x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal(qneg(x))).

In clause (1), one universal quantifier over x scopes over the conjunction of the two inequalities. Both inequalities hold at every point, not merely almost everywhere. The measurability assertions are ordinary Measurable assertions for real-valued functions on E. Integrable in clauses (4)–(5) means genuine real Bochner absolute integrability. Clauses (6)–(7) are real Bochner integrals with the default measure volume on E, as specified by the packet.

Both sides of each of clauses (8)–(9) are measures on E. Measure.bind integrates the G-indexed measures γ(O) against νpos or νneg respectively. For a measurable B ⊆ E, the first left-hand measure has value ∫⁻ O, γ(O)(B) ∂νpos and the second has value ∫⁻ O, γ(O)(B) ∂νneg. On the right, withDensity uses Euclidean volume on E as base measure and the displayed extended nonnegative density ENNReal.ofReal(qpos(x)) or ENNReal.ofReal(qneg(x)); its value at B is the corresponding extended nonnegative set integral over B. ENNReal.ofReal is nonnegative extended-real truncation of a real value. These extended integrals explain the measure constructors; they are distinct from the real integrals defining qpos and qneg and their displayed normalizations. The two equalities separately identify the positive-sign and negative-sign mixtures with their respective densities. They do not assert equality between the two mixtures or between qpos and qneg.

All the local definitions and the entire conjunction lie inside the quantifiers over n, hn, κ, and hκ. The measure μ depends on n; νpos and νneg depend on n through μ and their determinant-sign sets. The functions γ and p depend on n and κ, with O as their group argument and x additionally an argument of p. The functions qpos and qneg depend on n and κ through p and the respective fixed group measures. The final densities are functions on E with those same parameter dependencies. There are no existential or unspecified constants. The displayed thresholds and numerical constants are exactly 3, 4, 0, 1, −1, 2 and π, in the roles specified above. No source identity, source fidelity judgment, or proof claim is part of this reconstruction.
